summary: Built near Atikokan as a Cold War radar and lookout tower, moved to Fort Frances in 1972 and to the Sorting Gap Marina in 2009; summer access by pass.

facts.design: Radar and lookout tower with a square, red-and-white cupola

access.note: Summer only, when the Sorting Gap Marina is open; visitors buy a pass that gives the day's access code, according to the town.

visit.trail_note: Summer only. The town says visitors can walk up the tower with the day's code from a pass.

events.note: RCAF gap-filler radar programme begins; Pal Lake, near Atikokan, is one of its filler sites
Gap-filler programme cancelled in January 1964; the Pal Lake tower is sold to Ontario's Department of Lands and Forests
Moved from Pal Lake to Point Park in Fort Frances as a tourist attraction; opened on 1 July
Fort Frances Museum established; the tower operates as an attraction until 2002
Closed over building-code safety concerns (stair inclines and railings)
Moved from Point Park to the Sorting Gap Marina

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the tower to the 1930s as a fire lookout and radar tower. The marker places the Pal Lake tower in a 1959 to 1964 radar programme and says it may briefly have been a fire lookout. The story gives both accounts and does not pick one.
The marker and the town give 33 m (100 ft) for the tower; the marker's detail gives about 21 m (70 ft) for the Pal Lake radar tower. The 33 m figure is used for the structure as it stands now.

sources.title: Waterfront tower has military radar surveillance roots

notes_for_editor: Origin is disputed: the register says 1930s (fire lookout and radar tower); the marker says a 1959-64 RCAF gap-filler radar tower that may briefly have been a fire lookout. The story reports both. Heights differ (33 m / 100 ft vs about 70 ft). The marker's lookout classification is contested; the owner may want to decide whether this stays in scope. The town's landmarks page places the summer-pass sentence under its Hallett entry; the sentence reads as the lookout tower but confirm before a visit. Access is the least certain part: the latest source is an undated Times column that says access was stopped by COVID-19, and no source confirms the current season or pass. The separate record ca-on-fort-frances-lookout-tower-original gives coordinates 49.162669, -93.325948 in Kenora District, but the marker and the Times column place Pal Lake near Atikokan (Rainy River District; the column gives 48-47-45.5 N, 091-36-41 W). Those coordinates look wrong; that record was not edited. The register spells the town Atkikokan; the story uses Atikokan. No new photos were found.
